newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-ITALY STUN SPAIN TO REACH CUP SEMIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ITALY STUN SPAIN TO REACH CUP SEMIS.

text.p: Unfancied Italy dumped Spain out of the Davis Cup on Saturday by snatching an unassailable 3-0 lead in their world group quarter-final tie.
Omar Camporese and Diego Nargiso collapsed onto the court in an exhausted embrace after a three-hour 5-7 7-6 (7-0) 6-2 7-6 (7-5) victory over Javier Sanchez and Francisco Roig.

"These have been two fantastic days," said non-playing captain Adriano Panatta, who was raised shoulder-high by Nargiso and team official Luigi Rossi to cheers from the flag-waving Italian crowd packing the indoor arena.
"I am happy for them and I'm happy for myself. The semi-final is a great goal and we've reached it two years running. Now we're going to rest a bit," he said.
Italy were knocked out of the last four by France last year and went into the tie in Pesaro, on the Adriatic holiday coast, talking down their chances of victory.
They will play away to either Sweden or South Africa in the semifinal in September. Sweden led South Africa 2-1 after Saturday's doubles.
Australia guaranteed themselves a place in the other semifinal when Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge staked them to a 3-0 lead over the Czech Republic by winning the doubles in Adelaide.
They, too, will have to travel to play it against either the United States or the Netherlands. The U.S. team led 2-0 ahead of Satureday's doubles in California.
Asked about Italy's chances of going on to the final, which they won only in 1976, Panatta said:
He had been quoted in the Italian press as saying precisely that of their prospects against Spain, who fielded two players in the world's top 12 and had been highly favoured to win.
"The boys deserve respect. This is a very important victory for Italian tennis," Panatta said.
Veteran Camporese, who came from two sets down in his singles match against eighth-ranked Carlos Moya on Friday, showed visible emotion after his second victory in 24 hours.

"My experience in the Davis Cup helped me a lot. Moya has only ever played one cup match. I've matured a lot, otherwise I wouldn't have been able to come from two sets down to beat him yesterday," he said.
Camporese was written off by Italian media before Friday's singles. Once ranked 18th, he slid down the ratings to his current 156th after a serious elbow injury in 1992.
Camporese and Nargiso wasted two break points in the first set of Saturday's doubles and then seemed to lose their nerve.
A driving forehand from Sanchez, ranked 38, gave the Spaniards the first set 7-5.

But the Italian pairing, who had beaten Spain together in the Davis Cup in 1993, broke serve at the beginning of the second set and picked up their game for the remainder of the match, in the end winning comfortably.
Also on Friday, Italian number one Renzo Furlan overcame Albert Costa, ranked 12th, in another five-set singles. The teams will play two dead reverse singles matches on Sunday.
